primitives.name: Tournament with Rivalry
primitives.verbatim_quote: Draw­ ing on data from the National Football League (2009–2023) and a survey-based measure of rivalry, this study investigates how perceived rivalry in the competition influences performance and sabotage behavior.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_i': 'Absolute performance of team i (dimensionless)', 'R_{ij}': 'Perceived rivalry intensity between teams i and j (survey-based index)', 'X_{it}': 'Control variables (e.g., team quality, game context)', '\\delta_j': 'Team fixed effects (controls for time-invariant team characteristics)', '\\varepsilon_{ijt}': 'Error term'}
primitives.assumptions: Teams maximize expected utility, rivalry impacts linear and quadratic terms, fixed effects control for unobserved heterogeneity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When rivalry approaches extreme values, psychological stress may overwhelm rational utility maximization.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian updating framework where players infer opponent's type and rivalry strength, adjusting effort and sabotage strategies accordingly.
layer2.telemetry: Sabotage foul rates conditional on rivalry intensity and past interactions.

primitives.name: U-Shaped Rivalry Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: Moreover, we identify a u-shaped relationship between rivalry intensity and sabotage fouls: sabo­ tage is lowest at moderate rivalry levels but increases under both low and high ri­ valry.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{ijt}': 'Sabotage fouls by team i against team j in period t (count)', 'R_{ij}': 'Rivalry intensity (same definition as above)', 'X_{it}': 'Control variables including game stakes and home advantage', '\\phi_j': 'Team fixed effects for sabotage propensity', '\\nu_{ijt}': 'Error term'}
primitives.assumptions: Sabotage costs increase superlinearly with effort, moderate rivalry creates ambiguity about optimal strategy, extreme rivalry triggers either escalation or deterrence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At very high rivalry, coordination failures may reduce sabotage as teams focus on defensive stability.

layer2.mapping: Conformal prediction intervals for sabotage rates given observed rivalry levels, accounting for uncertainty in opponent behavior.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation of actual sabotage from predicted baseline under varying rivalry.

primitives.name: Performance-Sabotage Tradeoff
primitives.verbatim_quote: Overall, our findings indicate that contests against direct rivals can undermine performance while simultaneously fostering sabotage at high rivalry intensity.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Pi_i': 'Expected profit or utility of team i (monetary units)', 'p(E_i)': 'Performance payoff function (increasing in E_i)', 'c(S_{ij})': 'cost of sabotage (increasing convex in S_{ij})'}
primitives.assumptions: Teams face a budget constraint linking performance gains to sabotage costs, tradeoff exists unless sabotage is perfectly efficient.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sabotage becomes too costly or ineffective, the tradeoff disappears as performance dominates.

layer2.mapping: State-transition models where teams switch between cooperation and sabotage based on Bayesian beliefs about opponent types.
layer2.telemetry: Transition probabilities between cooperative and sabotaging states estimated from match-level data.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that rivalry introduces strategic interdependence beyond standard tournament theory. When rivals are perceived as asymmetrically strong or weak, agents engage in complex signaling games. At low rivalry, there is little incentive for sabotage; at high rivalry, fear of losing dominates and sabotage becomes a credible threat. The U-shape emerges because moderate rivalry creates ambiguity about the optimal strategy, leading to experimentation and increased variance in behavior. Failure occurs when agents fail to update their beliefs correctly, leading to over-sabotage or under-effort. The primitives map to GSI via conformal prediction of betting margins, and to GSE via Markov decision processes modeling state transitions between rivalry regimes.
